title: *MGT611 GDB SOLUTION*
text:
*MGT611 GDB SOLUTION*
**1. Bilal, Tariq, and Saad (Gold Price Prediction)**

* **Nature of the Agreement:** This is a **wagering agreement** (governed by Section 30 of the Contract Act, 1872). Both Bilal and Tariq have staked money on the outcome of an uncertain future event (the price of gold next Friday), where one stands to win and the other stands to lose, and neither has any genuine insurable or proprietary interest in the event beyond the bet itself.
* **Can Bilal sue Saad?** **No.** Under Section 30, agreements by way of wager are **void ab initio** (void from the beginning), and no suit can be brought to recover anything alleged to be won on a wager or entrusted to a stakeholder (Saad) to abide by the result of a wager. *(Note: Under Pakistani contract law principles, Bilal could at most attempt to recover his own Rs. 5,000 deposit if demanded before it was paid over, though he cannot sue to enforce the Rs. 10,000 winnings).*

---

**2. Sara and Komal (Rain on Wedding Day)**

* **Nature of the Agreement:** This is a **wagering agreement** disguised as a conditional promise (Section 30). Although phrased conditionally ("if and only if it rains"), it lacks the commercial or protective purpose of a valid contingent contract (like insurance); neither party has a real financial interest in the occurrence of rain itself, and the arrangement is purely a unilateral bet where Sara loses Rs. 5,000 if it rains and Komal gets nothing if it does not.
* **Enforceability:** **Unenforceable.** First, as a wagering agreement, it is **void** under Section 30. Second, even if viewed purely through the lens of a conditional obligation (Section 32), the specified uncertain event (rain on the wedding day) **did not happen**, so no liability ever arose on Sara's part. Komal has no legal right to demand the Rs. 5,000.

---

**3. Kamran and His Lawyer (Property Case "Success Fee")**

* **Is this a contingent contract?** **Yes** (assuming the underlying fee arrangement is not barred as champertous/unethical under local Bar Council rules). Under **Section 31** of the Contract Act, 1872, a contingent contract is a contract to do or not to do something if some event, collateral to such contract, does or does not happen. Here, Kamran's obligation to pay the extra Rs. 100,000 is strictly contingent upon the uncertain future event of winning the property case, where Kamran has a genuine underlying interest in the litigation.
* **Is the lawyer entitled to the success fee?** **No.** Under **Section 32**, a contingent contract to do anything if an uncertain future event happens **cannot be enforced by law unless and until that event has happened**. Because Kamran lost the case, the contingency failed, and the lawyer has no legal entitlement to the bonus fee.

---

**4. Zara, Ahmed, and Sohail (Sale of the Flat)**

* **Is this a contingent contract?** **Yes.** Under **Section 31**, Zara’s obligation to sell the flat to Ahmed is dependent upon an uncertain future event collateral to their agreement—namely, Sohail refusing to buy the flat.
* **Can Ahmed enforce it at this stage?** **No.** Under **Section 32**, a contract contingent upon the happening of an uncertain future event (Sohail's refusal) **cannot be enforced until that event actually occurs**. Since Sohail has not yet made a decision, the condition precedent remains unfulfilled, making Ahmed’s suit premature and legally unenforceable at this stage. *(It would only become enforceable if Sohail explicitly refuses, or becomes impossible/void under Section 32 if Sohail accepts and buys the flat).*
